_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. English-only. Keep activityId/version in sync with config.json.

markingScheme.criterion: States that when the diaphragm contracts and flattens (and the ribs rise) the space/volume inside the chest increases, quoting at least two of their own volume/pressure readings from the Investigation Record.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine readings from the student's own Breathe-the-Lungs trials that show volume rising and/or pressure falling (e.g. 'volume 95%, pressure low'); exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim such as 'the chest got bigger' with no actual readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that a bigger chest space lowers the air pressure inside the lungs (so lung pressure becomes lower than the air pressure outside the body).
markingScheme.accept: 'The pressure drops / goes down / becomes less than outside' — any wording showing bigger volume causes lower pressure.

markingScheme.criterion: States that air flows IN because air moves from higher pressure (outside the body) to lower pressure (inside the lungs), linking this to their readings.
markingScheme.accept: 'Air goes from high pressure to low pressure, so it rushes in'; a correct cause-and-effect link is enough.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'air goes in' without any mention of the pressure difference causing it.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies that exercising muscle cells need more oxygen (and/or glucose) so they can carry out more respiration to release more energy.
markingScheme.accept: 'The muscles need more oxygen to make more energy / to respire faster'; mentioning glucose as well is good but oxygen alone earns the mark.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that breathing faster and deeper moves more air in and out of the lungs, so more oxygen can be taken into the blood (and more carbon dioxide removed).
markingScheme.accept: Any statement that faster/deeper breathing increases the amount of air ventilated and so the oxygen taken in / CO2 breathed out.

markingScheme.criterion: Links the two clearly: the extra oxygen is carried to the muscle cells for the extra respiration that releases the energy they need, and the extra carbon dioxide produced is breathed out.
markingScheme.accept: A clear link from breathing more -> more oxygen to the muscles -> more respiration/energy; naming CO2 removal strengthens it but is not required for the mark if the oxygen->respiration link is complete.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating that you breathe harder without connecting it to respiration in the muscle cells.

levels.descriptor: No readings from the Investigation Record used, and no correct pressure/airflow reasoning.

One of the three analytic points met: either quotes real readings showing the chest/volume increased, OR explains volume increase lowers lung pressure, OR states air flows in from high to low pressure.
Two of the three analytic points met — e.g. quotes real readings and explains the pressure drop, but does not link it clearly to air flowing from high to low pressure.

All three analytic points present: quotes at least two of their own readings showing volume up / pressure down, explains that the bigger chest lowers lung pressure below outside pressure, and states air flows IN from higher to lower pressure.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No correct link between exercise, breathing and respiration.

One of the three analytic points met: identifies the muscles need more oxygen for more respiration/energy, OR that faster/deeper breathing moves more air, OR links breathing to respiration — only one of these.

Two of the three analytic points met — e.g. says muscles need more oxygen and that faster breathing takes in more air, but does not complete the link to respiration releasing the energy the muscles need.

All three analytic points present: muscle cells need more oxygen for more respiration/energy, faster and deeper breathing takes more oxygen into the blood (and removes more CO2), and the extra oxygen reaches the muscles for the respiration that releases the energy they need.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed; no correct scientific vocabulary.

Main meaning understandable, but organisation or precision is weak, or key scientific terms (diaphragm, pressure, alveoli, oxygen, respiration) are missing or misused. Do not deduct for minor spelling/grammar slips that do not harm meaning.
Clear, logically organised full sentences using correct scientific vocabulary, precise enough to follow easily. Minor spelling/grammar slips that do not affect meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria. The Explain marks ARE the use_of_evidence criterion and the Apply marks ARE the reasoning criterion (one-to-one); never award them twice. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Communication is judged holistically across both answers and never overlaps the content marks. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept'; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it makes the meaning unclear. Use the raw Investigation Record data (not just the student's summary) to verify any claim about their own readings. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
